intro.title: useDebounce
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useDebounce` that delays the update of a value until a specified time has passed without any new changes. You'll learn the core concept of debouncing, which helps optimize performance by preventing rapid, repeated function calls, like those from user input in a search box. The main technologies involved are React hooks, specifically `useState` and `useEffect`, along with JavaScript's `setTimeout` and `clearTimeout` functions. By the end, you'll understand how to implement and apply debouncing in your React applications to create smoother user experiences.
intro.usecase: The useDebounce pattern is essential in modern web applications to optimize performance and user experience. You'll see it implemented in search bars like those on e-commerce sites (Amazon, eBay) where typing triggers product suggestions without overwhelming the server with every keystroke. It's also crucial in dashboard filters where adjusting date ranges or metrics should update visualizations smoothly, and in form validation that checks username availability as users type. This technique prevents excessive API calls and ensures responsive interfaces in data-heavy applications.
